item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 231744
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM PDT Fri Oct 23 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Vance, located several hundred miles south-southwest of Acapulco,
Mexico.

Western Central Pacific:
An area of low pressure is forecast to form near the International
Date Line, several hundred miles west of Johnston Atoll late this
weekend or early next week. Environmental conditions could support
some slow development thereafter while the system moves generally
eastward to east-northeastward.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.

$$
Forecaster Beven

item.title: Hurricane Vance Public Advisory Number 10
item.description:
Issued at 300 PM CST Fri Oct 23 2026 
147 
WTPZ32 KNHC 232038
TCPEP2
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Vance Advisory Number  10
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP222026
300 PM CST Fri Oct 23 2026
 
...VANCE STRENGTHENING QUICKLY AND COULD BECOME A MAJOR HURRICANE
TONIGHT...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 300 PM CST...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...11.2N 102.3W
ABOUT 425 MI...685 KM SSW OF ACAPULCO MEXICO
ABOUT 555 MI...895 KM SSE OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...105 MPH...165 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 325 DEGREES AT 5 MPH...7 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...971 MB...28.68 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
Interests along the southwestern coast of Mexico should monitor the
progress of Vance.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 300 PM CST (2100 UTC), the center of Hurricane Vance was located
near latitude 11.2 North, longitude 102.3 West. Vance is moving
toward the northwest near 5 mph (7 km/h). A slow motion toward the
north-northwest or northwest is expected to continue through the
weekend.
 
Maximum sustained winds have increased to near 105 mph (165 km/h) 
with higher gusts.  Steady to rapid strengthening is expected 
through tonight, and Vance is forecast to become a major hurricane. 
After that, slow weakening is forecast to start on Saturday night
and continue through Sunday.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 35 miles (55 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 205 miles
(335 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 971 mb (28.68 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Vance are expected to begin affecting
portions of the coast of southern and southwestern Mexico this
weekend and continue into next week. These swells are likely to
cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please
consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 900 PM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Beven

item.title: Hurricane Vance Forecast Discussion Number 10
item.description:
Issued at 300 PM CST Fri Oct 23 2026 
ZCZC MIATCDEP2 ALL
TTAA00 KNHC DDHHMM
 
Hurricane Vance Discussion Number  10
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP222026
300 PM CST Fri Oct 23 2026

Vance has become better organized since the last advisory with the 
formation of a well-defined eye inside the central dense overcast. 
Satellite intensity estimates have increased to the 83-104 kt 
range, and based on these data the initial intensity is increased 
to 90 kt. Although the central features of the hurricane are better 
defined, the outer banding seen earlier has become fragmented, and 
arc clouds that suggest the presence of dry air are seen southwest 
of the CDO.

The intensity forecast is a low confidence roller coaster ride. The 
eye of Vance is moving over a pool of water featuring both colder 
sea surface temperatures (near 27C) and reduced oceanic heat 
content. This should soon bring the current intensification to a 
halt, although the intensity forecast calls for Vance to become a 
major hurricane before that happens. The center will be near or over 
the cold pool through 48 h, and during this time southwesterly 
vertical shear should increase over the hurricane. This combination 
should cause weakening, and it is possible that Vance could weaken 
more than forecast during this period.  After 48 h, Vance should 
move north of the cold pool, and the official forecast at that time 
calls for some re-intensification, following the scenario shown by 
the HAFS models. By 96-120 h, an additional increase in shear and 
possible land interaction should cause the hurricane to weaken yet 
again.  As noted in the previous advisory, a track to the right of 
the forecast track will keep the center over the colder water for a 
longer time, while a track to the left would reduce how much time 
the center spends over the cold pool. 

After the westward jog seen earlier today, Vance has resumed a 
northwestward motion of 325/4 kt.  The hurricane is currently being 
steered by a weak mid-level ridge over eastern Mexico and the 
eastern Pacific, and later in the forecast period it will come under 
the influence of a large mid- to upper-level trough over the western 
United States as well as the adjacent portions of northern Mexico 
and the northeastern Pacific. While the dynamical models agree on 
the general synoptic pattern, the track forecast is complicated by 
the possibilities of how strong and vertically stacked Vance will 
be. A stronger and more vertically stacked storm, especially as 
depicted in the GFS, will likely move slowly toward the 
north-northwest and north during the forecast period. On the other 
hand, the UKMET and Canadian models forecast Vance to be weaker and 
shear apart vertically, with the low-level center being steered more 
to the northwest before eventually turning northward.  While the 
current structure makes such a shearing apart unlikely in the short 
term, it is possible that Vance could shear apart between 24-48 h if 
it weakens more than forecast, and at that point it could turn more 
northwestward.  The forecast track leans toward Vance staying 
vertically coupled, and it is in the best overall agreement with the 
Google Deepmind ensemble mean, the HFIP Corrected Consensus, and the 
Florida State Superensemble. 
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
